title: Adobe — Browser File Manager Rehearsal
briefing: A Senior Frontend Gen Studio candidate reports a file-system design prompt during a December 2025–January 2026 loop. The March 11, 2026 report does not specify its detailed scope; this browser file-manager exercise is a Codematica adaptation. Design a file manager with folder navigation, search, rename, move, and upload. This exercise adapts a public candidate report; company attribution and interview details are not independently verified. The practice constraints and follow-ups are Codematica additions. Use your own timer and drawing tool: 45 minutes designing, 10 minutes handling follow-ups, and 5 minutes reviewing. No coding is required. Your design is not automatically graded; reflection text is transient. The related lesson contains the source and shared rubric.
objectives: Define stable file IDs, parent relationships, folder pagination, permissions, and upload state.
Draw tree navigation, folder contents, selection state, metadata requests, and a separate upload flow.
Explain lazy loading, bounded rendering, cache invalidation after moves, and partial failures. Do not assume a filename or path is a permanent identity.

prediction.prompt: Which area is most likely to expose a weakness in your first design?

options.label: An uncertain request outcome or recovery gap.
Performance or accessibility under the stated constraints.

steps.title: 0–7 minutes: clarify the scope
steps.instructions: Design a file manager with folder navigation, search, rename, move, and upload. Identify two main journeys, required devices, freshness, permissions, and exclusions. Separate requirements from assumptions.

steps.title: 7–20 minutes: draw the architecture
steps.instructions: Draw tree navigation, folder contents, selection state, metadata requests, and a separate upload flow. Assign state owners and component inputs/events. Include loading, empty, and error states.

steps.title: 20–30 minutes: define data and APIs
steps.instructions: Define stable file IDs, parent relationships, folder pagination, permissions, and upload state. Specify one read and one write, including identities, response fields, cache policy, and safe retry conditions.

steps.title: 30–45 minutes: trace behavior and recovery
steps.instructions: Trace one interaction from input to confirmed state, then fail a request. Explain lazy loading, bounded rendering, cache invalidation after moves, and partial failures. Do not assume a filename or path is a permanent identity.

steps.title: 45–55 minutes: handle follow-ups
steps.instructions: A folder contains 100,000 files. A selected file moves elsewhere. An upload fails halfway. Access is revoked while the folder is open. Pick the hardest case and show which decisions change. State any unresolved limits.

steps.title: 55–60 minutes: review your evidence
steps.instructions: Score scope, components, state and data, APIs and consistency, failure recovery, and quality and trade-offs. Use 0: missing, 1: mentioned, 2: explained with a concrete decision and consequence. Check only evidence you can show. Choose the weakest dimension and redraw it; this is not an employer hiring threshold.

evidenceChecklist.label: I stated the main journeys, assumptions, and exclusions.
I drew component responsibilities and interaction contracts.
I assigned state owners, stable identities, and invariants.
I defined reads, writes, caching, and reconciliation.
I traced one failure through usable recovery.
I defended accessibility, performance, measurement, and alternatives.
I separated stable file identity from paths and traced a move, failed upload, or access revocation.

extensionChallenge: Keep a selected file open while another user moves its parent folder and revokes access. Explain navigation, cache invalidation, and recovery.
